messages:
maya: Handoff for evening shift — I'm on until 20:00 PT, handing off to @ash afterwards. Quick summary from the RINF-2024 postmortem follow-ups:
- Remediation A: kv-cache memory cap increase (rolled)
- Remediation B: alert threshold tweak (pending)
- Long-term: memguard allocator work (tracking ticket)

I rolled the cap change to us-west-2 dedicated pools at 22:10 UTC. No rollbacks so far. Please verify the cache miss/error metrics for the next couple hours and keep an eye on OOM alerts.

ash: Thanks — taking handoff at 20:00 PT. Quick question: which service instance got the config?

maya: rolled to redwood-dedicated-prod-3, redwood-dedicated-prod-4 (canary then full). Command I used:
```bash
# reloaded config on the fleet
./opsctl apply-config --env prod --pool redwood-dedicated-prod-3 --file configs/kv-cache-cap.json
```
You can check rollout status with:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get deploy redwood-dedicated-prod-3 -o yaml | grep image
opsctl rollout status redwood-dedicated-prod-3
```

devon: I can cover until 06:00 PT if you need overnight validation. I'll watch kv_cache_miss_rate and memory.rss trends. Goal: miss_rate < 0.5% and no sustained RSS increase.

liam: I ran a quick metric check at 23:05 UTC — miss rate dropped from 1.2% -> 0.3% in the canary pool. No OOMs in the last 90m. Pushed an update to the alert in RINF-456 (threshold + runbook link) — https://redwood.internal/ops/tickets/RINF-456

ash: Sweet. I'm going to mark "alert updated" in the handoff doc. Who owns the memguard allocator follow-up? That was flagged as medium priority in the postmortem.

maya: Created RINF-789 for the memguard work, assigned to @liam, ETA end of next sprint. I put notes in the postmortem thread.

devon: small note — saw one short regression earlier today where a canary pod restarted twice around 18:40 UTC. Logs showed transient GC pressure but came back healthy. Not seeing it repeat after the cap change.

liam: I pulled the logs for 18:40, tail below:
```
2026-03-16T18:40:12Z redwood-dedicated-prod-3 kernel: Killed process 27411 (inference) total-vm: 2.4G, anon-rss: 1.9G
2026-03-16T18:40:12Z redwood-dedicated-prod-3 inference[27411]: ERROR: OOM triggered in allocator, freeing KV cache entries
2026-03-16T18:40:14Z redwood-dedicated-prod-3 inference[27411]: INFO: restart complete, warmup done
```
We saw the OOM before the cap change. After the roll it's stable.

ash: Good to know. I'll keep the pager escalation policy at default but will notify @platform if it spikes again overnight. devon — can you confirm alerting is wired to the oncall rotation?

devon: Yep — alert routes to eng-oncall -> primary -> secondary. I re-tested the routing from the alert console at 23:20 UTC.

oncall-bot: Reminder: nightly coverage swap scheduled at 04:00 PT tomorrow. If you need to swap, please update the oncall roster.

ash: One more follow-up — postmortem asks for a canary autoscale guard to avoid pack-thrashing. Is that a new ticket or part of RINF-789?

liam: I'll add a subtask under RINF-789 for autoscale guard (RINF-789-1). Will propose a design in PR by next Wed.

maya: Thanks team — leaving notes in the handoff doc and tagging the tickets. If anything urgent pops, @ash please escalate. Otherwise I'll check in tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Release note — 2026.3.16.22:10 applied to redwood-dedicated-prod-3 (kv-cache cap). Commit: a3f5b9c

ash: Got it. taking over now — ping me in thread for status updates.

devon: I'll post a quick status update at 02:30 PT and again at 05:30 PT.

liam: I'll follow up on RINF-789 tasks and post the design draft in the postmortem thread tomorrow.

maya: last: reopening note — if we see >3% miss_rate or any OOM after the roll, reopen RINF-2024 for investigation.

ash: copied. will reopen if needed.
